Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and great questions. Attaching a short worksheet (Helix_PO_Worksheet.xlsx) that maps common procurement paths to the decision owner and expected timeline. High-level answers below, plus suggested next steps so procurement can move fast: 

1) Card vs PO: Pilot customers frequently use card for low-dollar pilots. For anything above your finance threshold we do invoice/PO + standard commercial terms. If you need a vendor form + W9, we can get that out same day.

2) AWS Marketplace: We support AWS Marketplace Private Offers for customers who want marketplace billing and consolidated invoices. If you prefer direct PO with Redwood invoices, that works too — the two paths are functionally identical from an integration standpoint, it’s mostly a procurement preference.

3) Private/VPC: Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer-managed VPC in us-west-2. We will need network allowlists and an onboarding window for the private control plane.

Suggested next steps (mutual action plan):
- I: Attach the Helix_PO_Worksheet and our Redwood_AWS_Marketplace_Guide for procurement to review (attached).
- You: Share procurement contact and any vendor-form templates by EOD Thu (owner: Alex).
- Me: I’ll loop Ben (billing) for payment-rail specifics and Marissa (CS) for onboarding timing.
- Target: Align on billing path and sign PO/Private Offer within 2 weeks if ready.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min sync with procurement and finance this week — open to time suggestions.

Thanks,
Hannah
